Unsafe use: a constant scaling (8 * speed) is applied in fixed-width 32-bit arithmetic, wraps modulo 2^32 to 0 when speed > UINT_MAX/8, and the wrapped product is then used as the denominator of a division (tach period), so a nonzero user input becomes a zero divisor; representation-equivalents include subtraction/addition under/overflow to 0, right-shift truncation to 0, and narrowing casts of nonzero wider values. Consequence: integer division by zero -> kernel oops/DoS and stalled PM programming (reliability bug, not memory corruption). Transferable pattern: denominator = f(untrusted_value) where f applies unchecked fixed-width scaling before ''/'' or ''%'', while all checks validate f''s input instead of f''s output at division width.
